diagnostics.name: Test-function range under the stated normalization
diagnostics.scope: The printed negative rho0 range and derivative upper bound fail for values allowed by sup phi=0. A translated nonnegative potential would require a separate correction; no complete Hessian proof repair is certified.

diagnostics.name: Zero comparison in boundary stability
diagnostics.scope: Counterexample to Theorem 5.5 exactly as printed, for every delta>0. This is a literal quadratic substitution, not a refutation of the known boundary gradient theorem or an original admitted result.

diagnostics.name: Boundary comparison scale does not control the negative potential
diagnostics.scope: The printed V=sup|v|+sup phi+1 gives tau>1. Division by 1-tau then reverses the test direction and negative scaling cannot preserve the cone. The final proof retains V while the theorem states only ||v||.

diagnostics.name: Boundary upper obstacle normalization
diagnostics.scope: b has nonpositive boundary data and Delta b=-n but is positive inside. The printed b<=0 implication needs a larger constant shift; it does not refute the order phi<=b.

diagnostics.name: CLN is not domination by volume
diagnostics.scope: With a fixed smooth cutoff and sufficiently small fixed A, negative cutoff Hessians are uniformly controlled, giving global smooth omega-psh examples on a flat torus with common sup bounds. Their Hessian densities are unbounded. Proposition 3.1 as a uniform all-Borel-set volume domination is false; CLN controls mass with domain separation instead.

diagnostics.name: Layer-cake integral diverges at zero
diagnostics.scope: The printed integral from zero to infinity of C s^(-q) does not converge for q>1. A small-s mass bound would be separate; the false CLN volume estimate is not repaired by splitting the integral.

diagnostics.name: Reciprocal optimization reverses the inequality
diagnostics.scope: t<=C/cap implies t^(-q)>=(cap/C)^q, not the upper bound used in Proposition 5.3. The restriction 0<t<1 also prevents the proposed small-capacity optimization. This is a proof defect, not a counterexample to all valid capacity-volume theorems.

diagnostics.name: Finite extinction does not follow from the stated recursion
diagnostics.scope: Counterexample to Lemma 6.2 as stated, for all t,s>0. The estimate uses the ordinary exponential series and gives no finite extinction.

diagnostics.name: Repeated interpolation summands introduce an extra factor
diagnostics.scope: The displayed differentiation includes m equal summands in addition to its prefactor m. A fixed factor can be absorbed in later constants, but it is not the stated identity.
